skill.name: pubmed-database
skill.description: Build advanced PubMed searches and direct NCBI E-utilities REST workflows for biomedical literature discovery, batch retrieval, and citation management.
skill.summary: Build PubMed searches and E-utilities API workflows for biomedical literature review and citation retrieval.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Static findings are false positives caused by documentation examples, Markdown code fences, official NCBI endpoints, and PubMed API placeholders. No prompt injection, credential exfiltration, command execution, or reconnaissance intent was found in SKILL.md or references/api_reference.md. The skill uses external PubMed APIs by design, so users should protect API keys and follow NCBI rate limits.

remediation.issue: Placeholder API key examples may encourage unsafe key handling if copied directly.
remediation.suggestion: Tell users to load real NCBI API keys from a secret manager or environment variable and never commit them.

remediation.issue: Network access is core to the skill but could be clearer for users reviewing permissions.
remediation.suggestion: Add a short note that API workflows send search terms and identifiers to official NCBI E-utilities endpoints.

static_findings.snippet: Include the API key in requests using the `&api_key` parameter:
- Free full text: Add `AND free full text[sb]` to query
- Has abstract: Add `AND hasabstract[text]` to query
Grep pattern for query examples: `diabetes|cancer|cardiovascular|clinical trial|systematic review`
- Respect rate limits to avoid service disruption
- Export early and often to avoid losing search results

content.user_title: Search PubMed with Direct REST Workflows
content.value_statement: Biomedical literature searches often need precise syntax, reproducible filters, and careful API planning. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code build PubMed queries and NCBI E-utilities workflows.
actual_capabilities: Build Boolean PubMed queries with MeSH terms, field tags, date filters, and article type filters.
Explain PubMed search syntax for authors, journals, titles, abstracts, identifiers, and publication dates.
Plan ESearch, EFetch, ESummary, EPost, ELink, EInfo, EGQuery, ESpell, and ECitMatch workflows.
Design batch retrieval flows with history server use, pagination, rate limits, caching, and response formats.
Guide citation export choices for reference managers, MEDLINE records, XML, CSV, and abstracts.
limitations: PubMed usually provides citations and abstracts, not guaranteed full text access.
NCBI API rate limits and usage policies still apply to every workflow.
Users must supply and protect their own NCBI API keys for higher limits.
Medical interpretation and clinical decisions require qualified expert review.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Systematic Review Search
use_cases.description: Create reproducible PubMed searches with PICO terms, MeSH headings, synonyms, study design filters, and documented date limits.

use_cases.title: Refine Library Search Strategies
use_cases.description: Check field tags, Boolean logic, publication type filters, and search history combinations before sharing a strategy.

use_cases.title: Plan PubMed API Extraction
use_cases.description: Design E-utilities requests for search, batching, history server retrieval, citation export, caching, and rate-limit handling.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Basic PubMed Search
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a PubMed search for [topic] from [date range]. Include Boolean operators, MeSH terms, English language filtering, and abstract availability.

prompt_templates.title: Refine a Review Strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Improve this PubMed query for a systematic review: [query]. Add synonyms, MeSH headings, PICO structure, study type filters, and documentation notes.

prompt_templates.title: Plan API Retrieval
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an NCBI E-utilities workflow for [query]. Include ESearch, EFetch, batching, history server use, rate limits, and export format choices.

prompt_templates.title: Audit an Automation Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this PubMed automation plan: [workflow]. Identify risks in query design, batching, API key handling, caching, rate limits, and reproducibility.

output_examples.input: Find recent systematic reviews on type 2 diabetes treatment.
output_examples.output: A PubMed-ready search strategy with MeSH terms, title and abstract synonyms, date filters, article type filters, and refinement notes.

output_examples.input: Plan batch retrieval for 4,000 PubMed records.
output: Use ESearch with history server enabled to store matching records.
Retrieve records in controlled batches with EFetch and documented pagination.
Apply caching, rate limiting, and clear export format choices.

output_examples.input: Find citations related to a known PMID and export them.
output_examples.output: A citation discovery workflow using related articles, ELink options, identifier checks, and reference manager export guidance.

best_practices: Start broad, verify PubMed search translation, then add field tags and filters.
Combine MeSH headings with title and abstract synonyms for better recall.
Use history server, caching, and throttling for large API workflows.
anti_patterns: Do not paste real API keys into shared prompts, examples, or committed files.
Do not use one narrow query for a systematic review without documenting synonyms and dates.
Do not ignore NCBI rate limits when retrieving large result sets.

faq.question: Does this replace the PubMed website?
faq.answer: No. It helps construct searches and API workflows that users can run through PubMed or NCBI E-utilities.

faq.question: Does it provide full text articles?
faq.answer: No. PubMed often provides citations and abstracts. Full text depends on PubMed Central, publishers, or institutional access.

faq.question: Is an NCBI API key required?
faq.answer: No. An API key is optional, but it increases allowed request rates for E-utilities workflows.

faq.question: Can it help with systematic reviews?
faq.answer: Yes. It can structure PICO terms, MeSH headings, synonyms, filters, and reproducibility notes for review searches.

faq.question: Can it help export citations?
faq.answer: Yes. It can guide export choices such as NBIB, MEDLINE, XML, CSV, abstracts, and reference manager workflows.

faq.question: Does it make medical recommendations?
faq.answer: No. It supports literature discovery and data retrieval. Clinical interpretation requires qualified medical review.
